topic: Inductors, cores, crystals, RF packages and MMICs

questions.question: What is piezoelectricity?

choices.A: The ability of materials to generate electromagnetic waves of a certain frequency when voltage is applied
choices.B: A characteristic of materials that have an index of refraction which depends on the polarization of the electromagnetic wave passing through it
choices.C: A characteristic of materials that generate a voltage when stressed and that flex when a voltage is applied
choices.D: The ability of materials to generate voltage when an electromagnetic wave of a certain frequency is applied

questions.answer: A characteristic of materials that generate a voltage when stressed and that flex when a voltage is applied

questions.question: What is the equivalent circuit of a quartz crystal?

choices.A: Series RLC in parallel with a shunt C representing electrode and stray capacitance
choices.B: Parallel RLC, where C is the parallel combination of resonance capacitance of the crystal and electrode and stray capacitance
choices.C: Series RLC, where C is the parallel combination of resonance capacitance of the crystal and electrode and stray capacitance
choices.D: Parallel RLC, where C is the series combination of resonance capacitance of the crystal and electrode and stray capacitance

questions.answer: Series RLC in parallel with a shunt C representing electrode and stray capacitance

questions.question: Which of the following is an aspect of the piezoelectric effect?

choices.A: Mechanical deformation of material due to the application of a voltage
choices.B: Mechanical deformation of material due to the application of a magnetic field
choices.C: Generation of electrical energy in the presence of light
choices.D: Increased conductivity in the presence of light

questions.answer: Mechanical deformation of material due to the application of a voltage

questions.question: Why are cores of inductors and transformers sometimes constructed of thin layers?

choices.B: To reduce power loss from eddy currents in the core
choices.C: To increase the cutoff frequency by reducing capacitance
choices.D: To save cost by reducing the amount of magnetic material

questions.answer: To reduce power loss from eddy currents in the core

questions.question: How do ferrite and powdered iron compare for use in an inductor core?

choices.A: Ferrite cores generally have lower initial permeability
choices.B: Ferrite cores generally have better temperature stability
choices.C: Ferrite cores generally require fewer turns to produce a given inductance value
choices.D: Ferrite cores are easier to use with surface-mount technology

questions.answer: Ferrite cores generally require fewer turns to produce a given inductance value

questions.question: What core material property determines the inductance of an inductor?
Which of the following materials has the highest temperature stability of its magnetic characteristics?
What devices are commonly used as VHF and UHF parasitic suppressors at the input and output terminals of a transistor HF amplifier?
What is a primary advantage of using a toroidal core instead of a solenoidal core in an inductor?

choices.A: Toroidal cores confine most of the magnetic field within the core material
choices.B: Toroidal cores make it easier to couple the magnetic energy into other components
choices.D: Toroidal cores have lower Q characteristics

questions.answer: Toroidal cores confine most of the magnetic field within the core material

questions.question: Which type of core material decreases inductance when inserted into a coil?
What causes inductor saturation?

choices.A: Operation at too high a frequency
choices.B: Selecting a core with low permeability
choices.D: Selecting a core with excessive permittivity

questions.question: Why is gallium arsenide (GaAs) useful for semiconductor devices operating at UHF and higher frequencies?
Which of the following device packages is a through-hole type?
Which of the following materials supports the highest frequency of operation when used in MMICs?
Which is the most common input and output impedance of MMICs?
Which of the following noise figure values is typical of a low-noise UHF preamplifier?
What characteristics of MMICs make them a popular choice for VHF through microwave circuits?

choices.A: The ability to retrieve information from a single signal, even in the presence of other strong signals
choices.B: Extremely high Q factor and high stability over a wide temperature range
choices.C: Nearly infinite gain, very high input impedance, and very low output impedance
choices.D: Controlled gain, low noise figure, and constant input and output impedance over the specified frequency range

questions.answer: Controlled gain, low noise figure, and constant input and output impedance over the specified frequency range

questions.question: What type of transmission line is often used for connections to MMICs?
How is power supplied to the most common type of MMIC?

choices.A: Through a capacitor and RF choke connected to the amplifier input lead
choices.C: Through a resistor and/or RF choke connected to the amplifier output lead
choices.D: Directly to the bias voltage (Vcc) lead

questions.answer: Through a resistor and/or RF choke connected to the amplifier output lead

questions.question: Which of the following component package types have the least parasitic effects at frequencies above the HF range?
What advantage does surface-mount technology offer at RF compared to using through-hole components?

choices.C: Components have less parasitic inductance and capacitance

questions.question: What is a characteristic of DIP packaging used for integrated circuits?

choices.A: Extremely low stray capacitance (dielectrically isolated package)
choices.B: Extremely high resistance between pins (doubly insulated package)
choices.C: Two chips in each package (dual in package)
choices.D: Two rows of connecting pins on opposite sides of package (dual in-line package)

questions.answer: Two rows of connecting pins on opposite sides of package (dual in-line package)

questions.question: Why are DIP through-hole package ICs not typically used at UHF and higher frequencies?

choices.B: Epoxy coating is conductive above 300 MHz
choices.D: Unsuitable for combining analog and digital signals
